title: Zechariah Son of Jehoiada
lead: Zechariah, son of the priest Jehoiada, was stoned in the Temple court on King Joash's order for rebuking Judah's apostasy (2 Chronicles 24:20–22). His dying words, "May the LORD see it, and may he seek it out," made him a byword for innocent blood, and most interpreters hear him in Jesus' words about "the blood of Zechariah."

sections.b: Jesus spoke of the blood of the prophets "from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah" (Luke 11:51; Matthew 23:35). Abel's is the first murder in the Hebrew Bible (Genesis 4:8–10). Zechariah's is the last in the order the Talmud gives (Bava Batra 14b), which ends with Chronicles, though the Aleppo and Leningrad codices put Chronicles first among the Writings, and he was not the last prophet killed in time (Jeremiah 26:20–23). Matthew's "son of Berechiah" matches the prophet Zechariah (Zechariah 1:1), and readers have debated whether this reflects confusion, another Zechariah, or a scribe's addition. Jewish legend told that Zechariah's blood seethed in the Temple court until the Babylonian conquest (Babylonian Talmud Gittin 57b).
